STATIC NDK ZLIB: PROVENANCE/NOTICE REVIEW STATUS, NOT A FOUND INCOMPATIBILITY

libarchive-android 1.1.6 (d3ee9c472173fcaf28e737f59dd34ef6cf3d1c88) pins Android NDK 28.1.13356709 / r28b and links find_library(Z_LIBRARY libz.a). This is static code inclusion, not merely loading a device-provided libz.so.

The historical v1.10.0 arm64 native binary has deflate/inflate 1.3.0.1 strings and no libz.so DT_NEEDED. The exact linked libz.a source revision and its optimization notices remain unresolved.

Official r28b platform-prebuilts commit 35fbbcd449f03cbb515538d0572d564e9984ef13 has an obtainable sysroot NOTICE. Its zlib section instead names version 1.2.12, Copyright (C) 1995-2022 Jean-loup Gailly and Mark Adler. That discrepancy is preserved in evidence/; the older section is NOT represented as the complete notice for the linked 1.3.0.1 code.

The known official zlib terms permit use, alteration and redistribution for any purpose, including commercial applications. They prohibit misrepresenting origin, require altered source versions to be marked, and require the notice to remain in source distributions. They do not themselves impose a general binary attribution, corresponding-source or native byte-identical rebuild requirement. See NDK-R28B-ZLIB-REFERENCE-NOTICE.txt, preserved unchanged from the official r28b sysroot notice; its stated version is 1.2.12, not asserted to be the linked version.

The version/source mismatch is an open provenance/SBOM and applicable-notices question, NOT by itself proof of noncompliance, license incompatibility, or a mandatory release stop. Determine whether separately licensed optimization code adds notices, document the actual artifact mapping as available, and preserve known applicable conditions. Do not use the existing "Android supplies libz" sentence to imply no zlib code is distributed. No unattainable bit-identical native attestation is required by this proposal. No build, license choice or final legal clearance is claimed here.
